name: age
title: age
short: age 1.2.1 simple file encryption (age, age-keygen)
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream age by Filippo Valsorda and contributors)

name: amfora
title: Amfora
short: amfora 1.11.0 browser for Gemini space
description:
Amfora 1.11.0: a terminal browser for the Gemini protocol (small, text-only pages over TLS 1.3, no ads, no scripts). Start it from the menu, press Ctrl-L
or type a gemini:// address (for example gemini://geminiprotocol.net), Tab/Enter follow links, q quits, ? shows the keys. Servers are trusted on first use (TOFU).
Built for Maemo 5 with Go (static). Upstream: https://github.com/makew0rld/amfora
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream amfora by makeworld and contributors)

name: apt-n900
title: apt-n900
short: Friendly apt command (list --upgradable, search, show) over apt-get
description: Adds /usr/bin/apt with the commands of modern apt: apt update, apt list --upgradable, apt upgrade, apt install, apt search, apt show, apt files, apt owns, and apt tui (apt-tui: a dialog based menu to upgrade, search, install and remove). It only calls apt-get, apt-cache and dpkg-query: nothing of the system package manager is replaced.

name: apt-transport-curl
title: apt-transport-curl
short: apt over HTTPS with TLS 1.2/1.3 (through curl 8)
description:
Replaces the apt method /usr/lib/apt/methods/https (old libcurl with OpenSSL 0.9.8, TLS 1.0 only) by a script that runs /usr/bin/curl. Repositories on GitHub Pages and other modern HTTPS servers then work with apt and the Application Manager.
The original method is kept as https.distrib and restored when the package is removed. Certificates are always verified (CA bundle of the curl package); Acquire::https::Curl-Insecure "true" turns it off, Acquire::https::CaInfo selects another bundle.

name: bash5
title: Bash 5
short: GNU Bash 5.3 shell (next to the system bash 3.2)
description:
Modern Bash with associative arrays, mapfile, ${var@U}, printf %(...)T and so on.
Installed in /opt/bash5, started as bash5. The system /bin/bash 3.2 stays untouched.

name: bat
title: bat
short: bat 0.26.1 cat with syntax highlighting and line numbers
description:
bat 0.26.1: shows files like cat, but with syntax highlighting, line numbers and paging (bat script.py, bat -p README.md, bat --list-languages).
Built for Maemo 5 with Rust as a static binary, without the git markers of the margin. The pager is cat by default (the less of the phone has no colour support): set BAT_PAGER to change it. Needs a terminal with colours (the menu terminal has them).
Upstream: https://github.com/sharkdp/bat
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream bat by David Peter and contributors)

name: bf-interpreter
title: BF interpreter
short: Brainfuck interpreter
description:
A small Brainfuck interpreter written in C (command: bf file.bf). The tape grows when the program needs it.
An example is in /opt/bf-interpreter/share/examples/hello_world.bf.
Built for Maemo 5 (armel, glibc 2.5). Upstream and author: https://github.com/elPytel/BF_interpreter (MIT)

name: bt-kbmouse
title: Keyboard and mouse
short: Bluetooth keyboard and TrackPoint: layout, pointer, scrolling and settings
description:
Makes a Bluetooth keyboard with a TrackPoint (ThinkPad) usable: Shift, Caps Lock and AltGr, the Czech or US layout, a visible mouse pointer with
adjustable speed, scrolling with the middle button, clicks. A service starts with the X server and takes over the keyboard when it connects; the application
sets the speed, the layout and the pointer. Pair the keyboard first (see DOC/bluetooth-keyboard.md). Needs the patched evdev driver
xserver-xorg-input-evdev-mouse (extras-testing).

name: busybox37
title: BusyBox 1.37
short: BusyBox 1.37.0 (modern coreutils, ash, awk, sed, tar, ...)
description:
BusyBox 1.37.0 next to the system busybox 1.23. Applets are linked in /opt/busybox37/bin;
add that directory to PATH to use them. /usr/bin/busybox37 runs the multi-call binary.

name: ca-certs-n900
title: ca-certs-n900
short: Current Mozilla root certificates for MicroB and other Maemo programs
description:
The phone has root certificates from 2010 and lacks about 117 current ones (ISRG Root X1, DigiCert G2/G3, GlobalSign R3, USERTrust and others).
The package adds the missing ones to the private certificate domain ssl-ca of the user (the Maemo certificate manager, read by MicroB); the system domain common-ca is not changed. Removing the package removes exactly these certificates.
Note: MicroB speaks only TLS 1.0, so sites that disabled it still fail. Tool: ca-certs-n900 install|remove|status.

name: camel-lite-ssl3
title: Modest TLS 1.3 (camel-lite)
short: camel-lite with OpenSSL 3: Modest with TLS 1.2/1.3 (replaces the system library, reversible)
description: The mail library of the Modest e-mail client rebuilt with OpenSSL 3.5 (static) instead of the NSS 3.12 of the browser, which knows TLS 1.0 only. Servers such as Centrum (imap.centrum.cz, smtp.centrum.cz) then work in Modest. The system library is replaced by links, dpkg -r restores the originals. Restart Modest after install and remove.

name: cbonsai
title: cbonsai
short: Bonsai tree generator for the terminal
description:
cbonsai grows a random bonsai tree in the terminal. Run cbonsai -l to watch it grow,
cbonsai-live for an endless forest, cbonsai -h for the other options.
Built for Maemo 5 (armel, glibc 2.5) with ncursesw linked statically.
Upstream: https://gitlab.com/jallbrit/cbonsai

name: cmatrix
title: CMatrix
short: Matrix-style falling characters in the terminal
description:
cmatrix shows scrolling characters like in the movie The Matrix. Press q to quit.
Options: -b bold, -C <colour>, -s screensaver mode (any key quits), -u <0-10> speed.
Built for Maemo 5 (armel, glibc 2.5), dynamically linked against the system libncurses5.
Upstream: https://github.com/abishekvashok/cmatrix

name: curl
title: curl
short: Command line tool for transferring data with URLs (TLS 1.3)
description:
curl 8.23.0 with mbedTLS 3.6.7, built for Maemo 5. Supports HTTPS with TLS 1.2/1.3,
so it works with servers that the system OpenSSL 0.9.8 of the device cannot talk to.
Installed in /opt/curl, with a link /usr/bin/curl. Upstream: https://curl.se/

name: dialog
title: dialog
short: dialog 1.3-20260721: dialog boxes for shell scripts
description:
dialog 1.3-20260721: text-mode menus, check lists, input boxes, message boxes, file selectors and gauges for shell scripts (dialog --menu, --checklist, --msgbox, --inputbox, --yesno). Full options: dialog --help. Built for Maemo 5 with a static ncursesw (UTF-8, line drawing).
Upstream: https://invisible-island.net/dialog/
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream dialog by Thomas E. Dickey)

name: fd
title: fd
short: fd 10.5.2 simple, fast alternative to find
description:
fd 10.5.2: finds files by name with a regular expression, coloured output, respects .gitignore, skips hidden files and runs commands on the
results (fd -e png -x ls -l). Example: fd report ~/MyDocs   or   fd -e deb. Built for Maemo 5 with Rust as a static binary.
Upstream: https://github.com/sharkdp/fd
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream fd by David Peter and contributors)

name: file
title: file
short: file 5.48 file type detection
description:
file 5.48 for Maemo 5: tells the type of a file from its content (file -b --mime-type photo.jpg). The magic database is in /opt/file/share/misc/magic.mgc.
The file manager ranger uses it for files with an unknown extension (the package ranger has only a small stand-in: this one takes precedence in /usr/bin).
Compressed files are not looked into (no zlib/bzip2/xz in this build). Upstream: https://www.darwinsys.com/file/
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream file by Christos Zoulas and contributors)

name: fzf
title: fzf
short: fzf 0.75.0 fuzzy finder for the command line
description:
fzf 0.75.0: an interactive filter for lists. Pipe anything into it (ls | fzf, history | fzf, find . -type f | fzf), type a few letters of the
line you want and press Enter. With bash 5 the key bindings come from: eval "$(fzf --bash)" (Ctrl-R history, Ctrl-T files, Alt-C directories).
Built for Maemo 5 with Go (static, GOARM=7, the 2.6.28 kernel needs the patched toolchain of this project). Upstream: https://github.com/junegunn/fzf
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream fzf by Junegunn Choi and contributors)

name: git
title: git
short: Distributed version control system (modern, HTTPS over TLS 1.3)
description:
git 2.56.0 built for Maemo 5, linked with libcurl and mbedTLS so that it can clone from
HTTPS servers such as GitHub (the old git 1.6.2 of the device cannot). Installed in /opt/git,
replaces the git 1.6.2-1 package. Upstream: https://git-scm.com/

name: gpodder
title: gPodder Podcast Client
short: A podcast aggregator for the Nokia N900
description:
gPodder is a podcast receiver/catcher with a specialized UI that has been optimized for Maemo 5 and the N900.
Podcasts are like short radio shows that you can download from the Internet and subscribe to like blogs or news feeds.
Version 2.20.3 "The Odd Pod" built from the upstream git tag obsolete/maemo5, with HTTPS through curl and YouTube through yt-dlp.
Upstream: http://gpodder.org/
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream gPodder by Thomas Perl)

name: gurk
title: gurk (Signal)
short: gurk 0.10.2 Signal messenger client for the terminal
description:
gurk 0.10.2, a terminal client for the Signal messenger (a linked device of your account: scan the QR code on the first start).
Built for Maemo 5 with Rust as a static binary (TLS 1.3, SQLite with encryption), 23 MB. It needs about 7 MB of RAM when idle; the first
start is slow (keys, first synchronisation). Keys: Tab/arrows to move, F1 help, Ctrl-C quits. Data is stored in ~/.config/gurk and ~/.local/share/gurk.
Upstream: https://github.com/boxdot/gurk-rs
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream gurk-rs by boxdot and contributors)

name: htop3
title: htop 3
short: Interactive process viewer (htop 3.x)
description:
htop is an interactive process viewer. This is htop 3.x built for Maemo 5, installed in
/opt/htop3 next to the system htop 0.8.3. Start it with htop3 (refresh interval 5 s by default).
Upstream: https://github.com/htop-dev/htop

name: ical-sync
title: Calendar sync
short: Keep iCal calendars (Google Calendar, holidays) in the Maemo Calendar
description:
Follows iCal (.ics) addresses, for example the secret iCal address of a Google calendar or a public calendar, and keeps their events and
tasks in the Maemo Calendar: new items are added, changed ones replaced, removed ones deleted; the past is kept for at most a month, the future as far
as the feed goes. A job with cron checks every 30 minutes, only when the phone is online already (it never starts a connection), and updates each
calendar at its own interval. The application adds and removes the addresses, sets the interval and switches the log. The Czech public holidays are the
default calendar. Command line: ical-sync (see ical-sync --help). Upstream: this project (MIT).

name: irssi
title: irssi
short: irssi 1.4.5 IRC client
description:
irssi 1.4.5: the IRC client in the terminal. Start it in a terminal (irssi), then /connect -tls irc.libera.chat 6697, /join #channel,
/help lists the commands. TLS 1.2/1.3 works (OpenSSL 3, CA bundle of the curl package; keep the phone clock correct, ntp-sync).
Built for Maemo 5 with static GLib 2.66, OpenSSL 3 and ncursesw (UTF-8), no Perl. Upstream: https://irssi.org
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream irssi by the Irssi project)

name: jq
title: jq
short: Command-line JSON processor
description:
jq 1.8.2 built for Maemo 5 (armel, glibc 2.5). Filters and transforms JSON,
used for example with the Audiobookshelf API. Regular expressions via the bundled oniguruma.
Upstream: https://jqlang.org/

name: libsignal-purple
title: Signal (libpurple plugin)
short: Signal in the Maemo messaging UI (libpurple plugin over signal-bridge)
description:
A libpurple protocol plugin that shows Signal as an account in Settings > Accounts and the chats in Conversations. It does no cryptography: it talks to the signal-bridge daemon, which it starts when needed (first connection takes about a minute). The device must be linked first (for example with gurk); do not run gurk at the same time as the account is online.
Restart Mission Control or reboot after installing. Remove the package to undo (the haze.manager block is removed, a backup is kept as haze.manager.orig-signal).

name: links
title: Links
short: links 2.30 text web browser with TLS 1.3
description:
Links 2.30, a text mode web browser with menus, tables and frames, for Maemo 5. HTTPS uses a private static OpenSSL 3, so modern
sites (TLS 1.2/1.3) open, unlike in the stock browser. Start it from the menu or with: links https://example.org  (Esc opens the menu).
Certificates are verified against the bundled Mozilla CA list (/opt/links/etc/cacert.pem, override with SSL_CERT_FILE).
Upstream: http://links.twibright.com
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream Links by Mikulas Patocka and contributors)

name: mandoc
title: mandoc
short: man page viewer: man, apropos, whatis
description:
mandoc 1.14.6 built for Maemo 5 (armel, static). The phone has only the BusyBox man, which needs nroff and cannot show a page. This package formats man pages itself and
installs man, apropos, whatis and makewhatis in /usr/local/bin. The search path includes /opt/<package>/share/man of every package (set at login in /etc/profile.d/mandoc.sh).
Open a new terminal, then: man mandoc.
Upstream: https://mandoc.bsd.lv/ (ISC licence)

name: mc
title: Midnight Commander
short: mc 4.8.33 two-panel file manager
description:
Midnight Commander 4.8.33: file manager with two panels in the terminal (mc), the editor mcedit and the viewer mcview. Copy, move, search,
archives (tar, zip, ...) as directories, FTP and SMB are not built in. F-keys work in xterm; where they do not, use Esc followed by a digit (Esc 1 = F1).
Built for Maemo 5 with static GLib 2.66 and ncursesw (UTF-8), without X11, GPM, SFTP and NLS. Upstream: https://midnight-commander.org
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream mc by the Midnight Commander team)

name: micro
title: Micro
short: micro 2.0.15 terminal text editor with normal keys
description:
micro 2.0.15: a small editor for the terminal that works the way most people expect: Ctrl-S saves, Ctrl-Q quits, Ctrl-C/X/V copy, cut and
paste, Ctrl-F searches, Ctrl-E opens a command line (help, set, plugin), the mouse works. Syntax highlighting for many languages. An easier alternative to vim
and nano on the N900 (the Q key and the arrows are on the keyboard). Built for Maemo 5 with Go (static). Upstream: https://micro-editor.github.io
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream micro by Zachary Yedidia and contributors)

name: microb-nss
title: microb-nss
short: NSS 3.28 with TLS 1.2 for the MicroB browser
description:
Replaces NSPR 4.8 / NSS 3.12 of the MicroB engine by NSPR 4.16 / NSS 3.28.6 (TLS 1.2, AES-GCM, ChaCha20, SSL 3.0 off), so that sites that dropped TLS 1.0 open in the stock browser. The stock libraries are kept in /usr/lib/microb-engine-orig (dpkg-divert) and come back when the package is removed. Restart the browser daemon after installing or removing: /etc/init.d/tablet-browser-daemon.init restart.
Tool: /opt/microb-nss/bin/psm-sim host port (a TLS test that sets NSS up as MicroB does, run it with LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/microb-nss/lib).

name: msmtp
title: msmtp
short: msmtp 1.8.34 SMTP client (TLS 1.3), sendmail replacement
description:
msmtp 1.8.34 for Maemo 5 with OpenSSL 3. Sends mail through an SMTP server with login over TLS,
for example smtp.centrum.cz port 465. Mutt needs it because Mutt without Cyrus SASL cannot log in to SMTP.
Installed in /opt/msmtp, link /usr/bin/msmtp.

name: mutt
title: Mutt
short: Mutt 2.4.3 terminal e-mail client (IMAP/SMTP over TLS 1.3)
description:
Mutt 2.4.3 for Maemo 5 with OpenSSL 3, so it can talk to servers that require TLS 1.2 or newer
(for example Centrum). Replaces the old mutt 1.5.20. Installed in /opt/mutt, link /usr/bin/mutt.
Example configuration: /opt/mutt/share/doc/mutt/muttrc.centrum.example.

name: mutt-hildon
title: Mail (Mutt)
short: Hildon GUI for the Mutt/msmtp mail setup (IMAP over TLS 1.3)
description: Finger friendly mail client for Maemo 5: INBOX list, reading, reply and new message. Mail is read with curl (modern TLS) and sent with msmtp, the settings come from ~/.muttrc and ~/.msmtp-password. The menu item Open Mutt starts the full terminal client.

name: nano
title: nano
short: GNU nano 9.3 text editor for the terminal
description:
GNU nano 9.3 for Maemo 5: an easy console editor with on-screen shortcuts (^O save, ^X quit, ^G help).
UTF-8 text, syntax highlighting (/opt/nano/etc/nanorc) and the man page/info in /opt/nano/share. Built for armel, glibc 2.5.
Upstream: https://www.nano-editor.org

name: ncdu
title: ncdu
short: ncdu 1.22 disk usage browser
description:
ncdu 1.22 for Maemo 5: shows what takes the space on a disk, directory by directory (d deletes, q quits, ? help).
The menu entry scans /home/user; in a terminal: ncdu /opt, ncdu -x / (-x stays on one file system). Built for armel, glibc 2.5; ncurses comes from the phone.
Upstream: https://dev.yorhel.nl/ncdu
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream ncdu by Yoran Heling)

name: ntp-sync
title: ntp-sync
short: Set the clock over NTP (works without a SIM card)
description:
Sets the system clock and the RTC with the busybox ntpd. Runs automatically when a network connection comes up (at most every 10 minutes), or by hand: sudo ntp-sync.
ntp-sync -n only shows the offset. Servers: /etc/ntp-sync.conf.
The Maemo setting for automatic time uses the cellular network time (NITZ), not NTP.

name: openssh
title: OpenSSH 10.6p2
short: OpenSSH 10.6p2 client and server (modern ciphers, OpenSSL 3), alongside the system one
description:
OpenSSH 10.6p2 portable for Maemo 5 with a private static OpenSSL 3 and zlib, installed in /opt/openssh. The system OpenSSH 5.1 stays as it is.
Client: ssh-modern, scp-modern, sftp-modern, ssh-keygen-modern (ed25519 keys, modern key exchange, works with current servers).
Server: /opt/openssh/sbin/sshd on port 2222, keys only, no root login (see /opt/openssh/etc/sshd_config). It is not started by the package.
Not tested on a real N900 when it was packaged: the sandbox of sshd is the rlimit one (the 2.6.28 kernel has no seccomp filter).
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream OpenSSH by the OpenBSD project)

name: profanity
title: Profanity
short: Profanity 0.19.0 XMPP (Jabber) client
description:
Profanity 0.19.0: an XMPP (Jabber) client in the terminal. Start it in a terminal (profanity), then /connect user@server.example (it asks for the
password), /msg user@server hello, /join room@conference.server. /help lists the commands. TLS 1.2/1.3 (OpenSSL 3, CA bundle of the curl package; keep the
phone clock correct, ntp-sync). Built for Maemo 5 with static GLib, libstrophe, libcurl, SQLite, readline and ncursesw; no OMEMO, OTR, PGP or plugins.
Upstream: https://profanity-im.github.io
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream Profanity by James Booth and contributors)

name: purple-echo
title: purple-echo
short: Echo test protocol for the Maemo messaging UI (libpurple/haze)
description:
A test protocol (step 0 of the native Signal plan): a libpurple plugin with one contact, echo-bot, that answers every message with "Echo: <text>". It adds the protocol "Echo (test)" to telepathy-haze (haze.manager block, account profile, icon) to check that Settings > Accounts and Conversations show a protocol from a third-party plugin.
The Mission Control daemon reads the manager files at start: restart it or reboot after installing. Remove the package to undo (the haze.manager block is removed, a backup is kept as haze.manager.orig-echo).

name: python3-hildonlite
title: hildonlite (Python 3)
short: Hildon and GTK 2 windows from Python 3 (ctypes layer)
description:
Python module hildonlite: Window, Box, Label, Button, Entry (with completion), TextView, PannableArea, AppMenu, lists, dialogs and timers over GTK 2 and Hildon,
called through ctypes, because PyGTK exists only for Python 2 and PyGObject has no GTK 2 / Hildon typelibs.
Use: import hildonlite as hl. Examples: /opt/python3/share/doc/python3-hildonlite/examples. The same source installs with pip (pip install git+https://github.com/n900-resurrection/hildonlite).

name: python3.11
title: Python 3.11
short: Python 3.11.18 for Maemo 5 with TLS 1.3 (ssl), sqlite3, ctypes, readline and pip
description: Python 3.11.18 built for the N900 in /opt/python3 (links /usr/bin/python3, python3.11). The ssl module uses OpenSSL 3.5, certificates come from the curl package. pip is included (pip3). The system Python 2.5 stays untouched.

name: quickjs
title: QuickJS
short: Small JavaScript engine (ES2023), runtime for yt-dlp
description:
QuickJS 2026.06.04 built for Maemo 5 (armel, glibc 2.5): command qjs. Used by yt-dlp to solve the
JavaScript challenges of YouTube. Upstream: https://bellard.org/quickjs/

name: ranger
title: Ranger
short: ranger 1.9.4 console file manager
description:
ranger 1.9.4, a console file manager with VI key bindings, for Maemo 5. It runs on the Python 3.11 of the package python3.11.
Run ranger in the terminal (arrow keys or h j k l, q quits). Images, PDF, HTML, audio and video open in the applications of the phone (Image Viewer, PDF Viewer, Browser, Media Player), text in vim; only directories and plain text are previewed.
Upstream: https://ranger.fm/
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream ranger by Roman Zimbelmann and contributors)

name: ripgrep
title: ripgrep
short: ripgrep 15.2.0 fast recursive text search (rg)
description:
ripgrep 15.2.0 (rg): searches directories recursively for a regular expression, respects .gitignore, skips binary and hidden files, and is
much faster than grep -r. Example: rg -n 'TODO' ~/src   or   rg --files | rg png. Built for Maemo 5 with Rust as a static binary (without PCRE2).
Upstream: https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream ripgrep by Andrew Gallant and contributors)

name: rsync
title: rsync
short: rsync 3.5.2 file synchronisation over SSH
description:
rsync 3.5.2 for Maemo 5: copies and synchronises files and directories, sending only the differences (rsync -avz --progress ~/dir user@host:backup/).
It uses the ssh of the phone as the transport (the same rsync must be on the other side). Built for armel, glibc 2.5, without the optional compression
and checksum libraries. Upstream: https://rsync.samba.org
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream rsync by Andrew Tridgell, Wayne Davison and contributors)

name: screen
title: screen
short: GNU screen 5.0.2 terminal multiplexer
description:
GNU screen 5.0.2: several programs in one terminal, detach and reattach later (screen, Ctrl-A d to detach, screen -r to come back, Ctrl-A c a new window,
Ctrl-A n/p next/previous, Ctrl-A [ scrollback). An alternative to tmux for people who know it. Sockets go to ~/.screen. Defaults in /opt/screen/etc/screenrc.
Built for Maemo 5 with the ncurses of the phone. Upstream: https://www.gnu.org/software/screen

name: selfie
title: Selfie
short: Live preview of the front camera, a photo button and the camera button (test application)
description: Shows what the camera sees (front by default, a button switches to the back one) and saves a JPEG to ~/MyDocs/DCIM. Written in Python 3 with hildonlite and GStreamer through ctypes, it is mainly a test of the cameras. The camera has one reader: close the stock Camera application first.

name: sfeed
title: sfeed
short: sfeed 2.4 RSS/Atom feed and podcast reader for the terminal
description:
sfeed 2.4 for Maemo 5: small tools that parse RSS/Atom feeds into a plain format and a curses reader.
Feeds are fetched with curl over TLS 1.3. Run sfeed-reader. Podcasts are normal feeds, the audio link is in the enclosure field.

name: sfeed-hildon
title: Feed reader
short: Native RSS/Atom and podcast feed reader on top of sfeed
description:
A touch reader for RSS and Atom feeds (and the text of podcast episodes). The feeds are downloaded by sfeed_update with curl, so
modern HTTPS servers (TLS 1.2 and 1.3) work, where the stock RSS reader and Feed Circuit fail with a TLS error. The application lists the feeds
with the number of new items, the items of a feed or all unread ones, shows the text of an item, opens its link in the browser, adds and removes
feeds (the list is ~/.sfeed/sfeedrc, shared with the terminal reader sfeed-reader), imports OPML and remembers what was read in the file that sfeed_markread uses.
A job with cron (every 30 minutes, only when the phone is online already) can update the feeds in the background; the interval is set in the application.
Upstream: this project (MIT).

name: signal-bridge
title: signal-bridge
short: Signal daemon (presage) with a local socket, for the messaging UI plugin
description:
signal-bridge 0.1.0: a daemon built on presage that serves a local unix socket (~/.local/share/signal-bridge/bridge.sock) with a simple line protocol. The package libsignal-purple uses it to show Signal in the Maemo messaging UI. It opens the store of an already linked device (the one of gurk: link the device with gurk first); do not run gurk and the daemon at the same time. Start by hand: signal-bridge-start (log: ~/.local/share/signal-bridge/daemon.log); commands: signal-bridge contacts, groups, whoami, messages.
Static ARMv7 musl binary. Upstream presage: https://github.com/whisperfish/presage (AGPL-3.0).

name: smb
title: SMB client
short: SMB2/SMB3 command-line client (ls, get, put, ...)
description:
Small client for Windows/Samba/NAS shares over SMB 2 and 3 (NTLMSSP, signing and
encryption of SMB 3), built on libsmb2 6.3 and statically linked. Commands: ls, get,
put, rm, mkdir, rmdir, mv, stat, df. No SMB 1 and no kernel mount (the kernel has no cifs).
Usage: smb ls smb://host/share/ ; smb -u user get smb://host/share/file

name: strace
title: strace
short: strace 6.19 system call tracer
description:
strace 6.19 for Maemo 5: shows the system calls and signals of a program (strace -f -o /tmp/out.txt command; strace -p PID).
Useful when an application hangs or fails without a message. Built for armel (native ABI only), glibc 2.5.
Upstream: https://strace.io
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream strace by the strace project)

name: terminfo-256color
title: terminfo-256color
short: Terminfo for 256-colour terminals (xterm-256color, screen-256color, tmux-256color)
description:
The phone has only 8-colour terminfo entries, so programs that use more colours (ranger, cbonsai, tmux, vim with a colour scheme) fail with: Color number is greater than COLORS-1 (7).
Adds xterm-256color, screen-256color and tmux-256color to /usr/share/terminfo (no system file is replaced). The package adds a small block to /home/user/.bashrc that switches TERM=xterm to xterm-256color (removed with the package); other shells: export TERM=xterm-256color

name: tig
title: tig
short: tig 2.6.1 text-mode interface for git
description:
tig 2.6.1: browse the history of a git repository, diffs, files and branches, stage changes line by line. Run it in a repository (tig, tig status,
tig blame file, tig show). Keys: Enter opens, q closes, h shows the help. It uses the git of this repository's git package (modern git with HTTPS).
Built for Maemo 5 with a static ncursesw (UTF-8). Upstream: https://jonas.github.io/tig
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream tig by Jonas Fonseca and contributors)

name: tiny
title: TINY
short: A quiz robot: a tiny neural network with a robot voice
description:
TINY 2.1 is a question answering neural network with 367,000 weights that reads and writes letter by letter and knows about 3,500 facts (countries, elements, animals, sums, words in other languages). Outside them it makes answers up. It has a full-screen terminal interface with a live neural monitor and a robot voice. Port of the DOS program to the N900: the screen follows the size of the terminal.
Keys: PgUp / PgDn volume, Ctrl-A help, Ctrl-S sound, Ctrl-V voice, Ctrl-T creativity, Esc quit.
Upstream: https://github.com/WollyMonjac/Tiny-2.1 (port: https://github.com/n900-resurrection/Tiny-2.1)

name: tmux
title: tmux
short: tmux 3.8 terminal multiplexer
description:
tmux 3.8 for Maemo 5: several terminal windows and panes in one screen, sessions that survive a closed terminal or a lost SSH connection.
Prefix key Ctrl-b (c new window, n/p next/previous, % and " split, d detach, tmux attach returns). libevent is built in, ncurses comes from the phone.
Upstream: https://github.com/tmux/tmux
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream tmux by Nicholas Marriott and contributors)

name: tty-clock
title: tty-clock
short: Digital clock for the terminal
description:
tty-clock shows a large digital clock in the terminal. Options: -s seconds, -c centered,
-C <0-7> colour, -t 12 hour format, -b bold, -d <ms> refresh delay.
Built for Maemo 5 (armel, glibc 2.5), dynamically linked against the system libncurses5.
Upstream: https://github.com/xorg62/tty-clock

name: vim9
title: Vim 9
short: Vim 9.2.1302 text editor for the terminal (command vim9)
description:
Vim 9 for Maemo 5 next to the system vim 7.2: the command is vim9 (the system vim and vi stay untouched). Normal features,
UTF-8, syntax highlighting, no GUI and no scripting languages. The tool xxd is xxd9. Built for armel, glibc 2.5.
Settings: /opt/vim9/share/vim/vimrc (the mouse is off), personal ~/.vimrc. Upstream: https://www.vim.org

name: weechat
title: WeeChat
short: WeeChat 4.10.4 chat client (IRC)
description:
WeeChat 4.10.4: an extensible chat client in the terminal. Start it in a terminal (weechat), then /server add libera irc.libera.chat/6697 -tls,
/connect libera, /join #channel. /help lists the commands. TLS 1.2/1.3 (GnuTLS, CA bundle of the curl package; keep the phone clock correct, ntp-sync).
Built for Maemo 5 with static GnuTLS, libgcrypt, libcurl and ncursesw (UTF-8); no scripting languages, no relay, no spell checker. Upstream: https://weechat.org
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream WeeChat by Sébastien Helleu)

name: wget
title: Wget
short: GNU Wget 1.25.0 (HTTPS with TLS 1.3)
description:
GNU Wget 1.25.0 for Maemo 5, linked with OpenSSL 3. Upgrades wget 1.10.2 of the device.
Installed in /opt/wget, with a link /usr/bin/wget. Certificates: /opt/curl/etc/ssl/cacert.pem.

name: whiptail
title: whiptail
short: whiptail (newt 0.52.25): dialog boxes for shell scripts
description:
whiptail from newt 0.52.25: text-mode menus, check lists, input boxes, message boxes and gauges for shell scripts (whiptail --menu, --checklist, --msgbox, --inputbox, --yesno), compatible with the common dialog options. Small: slang and popt are linked statically.
Upstream: https://pagure.io/newt
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream newt by Red Hat and contributors)

name: wireguard-go
title: WireGuard (wireguard-go)
short: wireguard-go 0.0.20250522: WireGuard VPN in user space, with wg and wg-n900
description:
WireGuard VPN for the N900: wireguard-go 0.0.20250522 (the Go implementation, static) with the wg tool and the helper wg-n900 up|down, which sets
up the interface and routes with the busybox ip of the phone. The kernel 2.6.28 has no WireGuard module, so everything runs in user space over /dev/net/tun.
Needs a WireGuard server (a home router, a VPS). See /opt/wireguard-go/share/doc/wireguard-go/README.Maemo. Upstream: https://www.wireguard.com
maintainer: elPytel (build of upstream wireguard-go and wireguard-tools by Jason A. Donenfeld)

name: wordgrinder
title: WordGrinder
short: Console word processor
description:
WordGrinder is a simple, Unicode-aware word processor that runs on the console.
Built for Maemo 5 (armel, glibc 2.5) with ncursesw linked statically.
Upstream: https://github.com/davidgiven/wordgrinder

name: xml-tools
title: XML tools
short: xmllint and xsltproc (libxml2 2.15.4, libxslt 1.1.45)
description:
Command-line XML tools built for Maemo 5 (armel, glibc 2.5), statically linked:
xmllint (well-formedness, XPath, pretty-printing, schema validation) and xsltproc (XSLT 1.0 with EXSLT).
The system libxml2 2.6.32 stays untouched.
Upstream: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2
